headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Airbyte’s broad egress can feed sensitive business data into Kotaemon’s document/chat pipeline without default verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, so prompt injection is not default. However, Airbyte can move content via APIs and broad egress, and Kotaemon ingests documents/chat transcripts through a web UI and file workspace. If Airbyte-fed content is manually or operationally bridged into Kotaemon, malicious instructions could ride along. The pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs are copied into Kotaemon inputs without sanitization, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared workspace or manual handoff is introduced, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste policy for any transferred text.
Add a one-line provenance label before importing content.
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted exports.
requires-engineering: add content sanitization and instruction stripping at the handoff point.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and calls third-party LLM APIs by default. If Airbyte-managed business data is routed into Kotaemon, sensitive content can leave the local boundary through model calls. The pairwise leakage path is credible even though a shared workspace is not explicitly documented.
conditions: IF business data from Airbyte is loaded into Kotaemon, that data may be transmitted to external model APIs.
IF Kotaemon is configured with hosted providers, file contents can be exposed beyond the local environment.
mitigations: Keep Airbyte outputs out of Kotaemon unless redacted.
Use a local-only model backend in Kotaemon.
Restrict Kotaemon to non-sensitive documents.
Rotate any API keys that may appear in imported files.
requires-engineering: enforce per-dataset egress controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte exposes API access and broad egress, while Kotaemon has a local file workspace and supports multiple instances. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, so direct conflict is not default. Uncertainty remains because shared orchestration or filesystem placement is undocumented, so the safer low severity is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, write conflicts become possible.
IF an orchestrator shares mutable credentials or state between them, collisions can occur.
mitigations: Place each agent in its own directory.
Avoid sharing OAuth tokens or API keys between agents.
Run only one writer per dataset at a time.
requires-engineering: add file locking or transactional coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce transformed business data, and Kotaemon is a RAG/chat system that can render citations and answers from ingested content. If Kotaemon treats Airbyte outputs as authoritative without verification, upstream extraction or sync errors can cascade into incorrect downstream answers or actions. The pair is not documented as integrated, so this is inferred but still plausible.
conditions: IF Airbyte exports are ingested into Kotaemon without validation, upstream errors can propagate.
IF Kotaemon is used to answer operational questions from those exports, incorrect outputs can be acted on.
mitigations: Validate Airbyte exports before ingestion.
Require human review for high-impact answers.
Tag imported data with source and freshness metadata.
Use a checksum or row-count reconciliation step.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data, while Kotaemon handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and sends content to external model providers. If regulated or confidential business data is routed from Airbyte into Kotaemon, retention and residency obligations may diverge from the source system’s expectations. The profiles do not specify certifications, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated business data is imported from Airbyte into Kotaemon, compliance obligations may change.
IF hosted LLM providers are enabled, retention and residency controls may differ from the source system.
mitigations: Exclude regulated datasets from Kotaemon.
Use a local model for sensitive material.
Document retention settings for imported files.
Review vendor DPAs before enabling hosted APIs.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
